The generic synthetic-rubber label refers specifically to a formulated EPDM elastomer/profile for technical seals, not pure unvulcanised rubber, SBR, natural rubber or any other elastomer. Both records describe polymer/elastomer production, internal mixing, extrusion and salt vulcanisation, including fillers/auxiliaries and internal transport. Their nominal PE/PP proxy inputs, carbon black and process electricity agree (0.251,0.0628,0.369 kg and0.719 kWh per product kg). These are inherited formulation/model quantities, not proof of identical actual EPDM chemistry or a new polymerisation recipe. Do not add another main polymer, carbon black, oil, extrusion or vulcanisation step, rescale to pure-polymer content or remove the caller separately listed processes.

The source mineral chain is internally ambiguous: packed-milled-lime suppliers lead to loose-product text calling it quicklime, but their actual production inventories take crushed limestone one-for-one and describe milling/sieving/packing without a calcination step. Native instead explicitly buys packed milled limestone. The nominal0.0883kg mineral quantity is retained inside the complete compound proxy; record the source naming/text-versus-inventory conflict rather than assert proven CaO-to-CaCO3 chemistry, add an invented kiln/CO2 or authorize a standalone lime/limestone conversion. Native/source packing, heat, geography and mineral grade can differ.
